title: Hack Back Work Interruptions
coreMove: Make focus and interruptibility legible at work so people know when to wait, reroute, or interrupt for true urgency.
sourcePressure: The chapter converts trigger judgment into negotiated work norms, treating interruptions as shared-system events rather than coworker flaws.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would blame coworkers instead of designing visible norms for shared attention.

hook: Hack Back Work Interruptions as a labeled topic opener
counterintuition: phones are not the problem by itself
tryThisNow: set a timer and notice your distractions
examples: reused old-package object-anchor shell from earlier Indistractable run

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital sterile-processing team handling instrument questions
exampleSpecs.audience: technician whose checks get broken by hallway questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: sterile tray errors can delay surgery
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the team agrees that blue cart tags mean wait unless a missing tray is already in the operating room
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A blue cart tag hangs from a sealed instrument tray.

exampleSpecs.domain: architecture model shop protecting laser-cutter setup
exampleSpecs.stakes: one casual question can ruin scale accuracy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places a red acrylic block on the cutter bench and posts the two times she will answer design questions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A red acrylic block sits beside a scale model base.

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal snowplow dispatch during route planning
exampleSpecs.audience: dispatcher pulled into side requests before a storm
exampleSpecs.stakes: routes get patched badly if every request sounds immediate
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he creates a storm-board column for true hazards and a second column for later complaints
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A snow route board is divided with black magnetic strips.

exampleSpecs.domain: textile mill quality team reducing floor interruptions
exampleSpecs.audience: inspector who gets stopped mid-defect count
exampleSpecs.stakes: counts lose reliability when every loom issue interrupts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they install a defect-card drop box and reserve immediate calls for snapped warp threads
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A defect-card box is bolted beside a loom counter.

exampleSpecs.domain: radio newsroom producer protecting edit time
exampleSpecs.audience: producer interrupted by every possible segment idea
exampleSpecs.stakes: the lead story misses air if edit time stays invisible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before, ideas arrive at the booth door; after, a rundown slot and emergency phrase govern interruptions
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A rundown sheet is clipped to a studio booth window.

exampleSpecs.domain: veterinary surgery desk routing nonurgent questions
exampleSpecs.audience: surgical nurse whose prep is interrupted by front-desk questions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she posts a prep-in-progress sign and names the one question that still comes through
exampleSpecs.firstImage: An anesthesia checklist rests beside a prep-in-progress sign.
